title: Enrolments in five batches
intro: A coaching institute runs five batches, A, B, C, D and E. The table shows the number of students who enrolled in each batch in each of four months, with each batch's four-month total and each month's total over all five batches. Eight entries are missing.
Additional information is given below the table.
clues: Each of the 20 monthly figures in the table (excluding the totals), including each missing one, is a multiple of 5 from 10 to 60, inclusive.
In each month, no two batches had the same number of enrolments.
Batch C's enrolments rose every month.
In April, batch B had the second-highest number of enrolments.

questions.stem: How many students enrolled in batch D in January?
why: C's row: 15 + Feb + 35 + Apr = 125, so Feb + Apr = 75, with 15 < Feb < 35 < Apr (fact 3). As multiples of 5 within 10 to 60, (Feb, Apr) is (20, 55) or (25, 50).
April's column: 25 + B + C + D + 35 = 205, so B + C + D = 145 in April. B's row gives B Feb + B Apr = 95, and D's row gives D Jan + D Apr = 95.

Try C = 50 in April: then B + D = 95. If B is 45 or less, D is 50 or more, so C and D both stand above B. If B is 55 or more, D is 40 or less and B is the highest. B = 50 ties with C. None leaves B second (facts 2 and 4). So C = 55, and B + D = 90 with B second: B = 50, D = 40.
So C's February is 20, and D's January is 95 − 40 = 55.

questions.stem: In how many of the four months did batch E have more enrolments than batch A?
why: January's column: A + 25 + 15 + 55 + 30 = 165 gives A Jan = 40, and A's row then gives A Feb = 150 − 40 − 50 − 25 = 35.
E is ahead in February and April only: 2 months.

questions.stem: What percentage of all April enrolments was accounted for by batches B and D together, to the nearest integer?
why: In April, B had 50 and D had 40, out of 205 in all.
90 ÷ 205 = 43.9%, which is 44 to the nearest integer.

questions.stem: Taking each batch's best month, what was the highest share of a batch's own four-month total enrolled in a single month?
why: Each batch's largest month over its own total: A 50 of 150 (33.3%), B 50 of 150 (33.3%), C 55 of 125 (44.0%), D 55 of 145 (37.9%), E 50 of 160 (31.3%).
The highest is C's April, 44.0%.
D also had 55 in a month, but over a larger total: the largest single entry is not the largest share.

questions.stem: If the information in point 4 were not available, and everything else stayed the same, which of the following could NOT be batch B's enrolment in February?
why: Without fact 4, the totals and facts 1 to 3 allow four ways to fill the table, and B's February entry is 40, 45 or 55 in them.

B Feb = 35 would need A Feb + C Feb = 180 − 35 − 30 − 50 = 65 and B Apr = 150 − 25 − 30 − 35 = 60. Working through C's two options, either D's January leaves the 10 to 60 range or D's April becomes 35, tying with E's April.
So 35 is the one value B's February entry cannot take. 40, 45 and 55 each appear in a fill that keeps every fact but the fourth.

steps: Write each row's and column's missing sum first. A: Jan + Feb = 75. B: Feb + Apr = 95. C: Feb + Apr = 75. D: Jan + Apr = 95. January: A + D = 95. February: A + B + C = 100. April: B + C + D = 145.
Batch C rises every month (fact 3): 15 < Feb < 35 < Apr with Feb + Apr = 75, so (Feb, Apr) is (20, 55) or (25, 50).
Fact 4 settles April: B must be second-highest, so C takes 55 and B 50, and D gets 145 − 105 = 40. Then C Feb = 20.
Every other blank follows from a sum: B Feb = 95 − 50 = 45, D Jan = 95 − 40 = 55, A Jan = 95 − 55 = 40, A Feb = 75 − 40 = 35.
Check fact 2, month by month: January 40, 25, 15, 55, 30; February 35, 45, 20, 30, 50; March 50, 30, 35, 20, 45; April 25, 50, 55, 40, 35. No ties: the table fills exactly one way.

title: Monsoon 2025: normal, actual and departure
cite: India Meteorological Department, 'Salient features of the monsoon 2025', rainfall for June to September 2025 by region; normal = long period average. Figures as published. The questions are ours.
intro: The table shows the June to September 2025 rainfall of four regions of India and of India as a whole: the normal (the long-period average), the actual rainfall, and the departure of the actual from the normal. Four entries are hidden.
The All India row is for the whole country; it is not the sum or the simple average of the four regions.
clues: Departure = (Actual − Normal) ÷ Normal × 100, published rounded to the nearest whole percent; a value exactly halfway between two whole numbers is rounded away from zero (so +26.5 is shown as +27 and −20.5 as −21).
Every rainfall figure printed in the table is exact. A hidden value is exact but unknown, and must be consistent with the other numbers in its row.
A 'minimum possible' or 'smallest' value is the least value consistent with the table. A bound that is approached but never reached counts as reached for answers rounded to the nearest integer.

questions.stem: What is the minimum possible actual rainfall of North West India, in mm? Give your answer to the nearest integer.
why: +27 means the true departure d has 26.5 ≤ d < 27.5 (26.5 is shown as 27, rounding away from zero).
The actual is least at d = 26.5: 587.6 × 1.265 = 743.31, so 743.

questions.stem: Which one of the following CANNOT be the normal rainfall of South Peninsula (in mm)?
why: 720 is outside: it gives a departure of 9.36%, shown as +9. 719 gives 9.51%, shown as +10, so it can be the normal; 714 and 716 are inside too.

questions.stem: What is the minimum possible value, to the nearest integer, of the sum of the actual rainfalls (in mm) of North West India, Central India, East & North East India and South Peninsula?
why: Only two actuals are hidden. North West is least at 743.31 (question 1). For East & North East, −20 means −20.5 < d ≤ −19.5 (−20.5 would be shown as −21), so its actual approaches 1,367.3 × 0.795 = 1,087.00 without reaching it; clue 3 counts it.
3753 takes the printed departures as exact; 3750 lowers only North West; 3757 takes East & North East at −19.5, its largest actual, not its smallest.

questions.stem: In how many of the four regions (excluding All India) is the actual rainfall certain to be at least 10% above the normal?
why: North West: at least 26.5% above. Central: (1,125.3 − 978.0) ÷ 978.0 = 15.06% above. Both certain.
South Peninsula's +10 can come from any departure from 9.5% up, so it is not certain. East & North East is below normal. So 2.

questions.stem: If East & North East India had received exactly its normal rainfall, by how many mm would its rainfall have been higher than its actual rainfall? Give the smallest possible value, to the nearest integer.
why: The difference is normal − actual, smallest when the actual is largest. −20 allows d up to −19.5 (−19.5 is shown as −20), so the largest actual is 1,367.3 × 0.805 = 1,100.68.

steps: A shown departure is a range: +27 means 26.5 to just under 27.5; −20 means just above −20.5 up to −19.5 (halves round away from zero, clue 1).

Each hidden value is then a range: North West's actual 743.3 to just under 749.2; Central's departure 15.06%, shown as +15; East & North East's actual above 1,087.0 up to 1,100.7; South Peninsula's normal above 712.6 up to 719.1.
A 'minimum possible' answer takes each range at its low end, even when the end is only approached (clue 3).
